summary: Richard P. Hayes is a scholar in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. He earned his doctorate at the University of Toronto under Bimal Krishna Matilal, also studying under Shoryu Katsura and T. Venkatacharya. He held posts at Toronto, McGill, and New Mexico.

Richard Payne works in history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He served as dean at the Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 1996, 2007) and held positions at the University of Chicago (attested 2021) and Numata Center.
Richard Peter Hottelet studied Buddhist studies under Narayan Hemandas Samtani and held a post at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (attested 1971).

Richard Phené Spiers was a scholar in history and archaeology. He studied at King's College London from circa 1855 to 1858 and at the École nationale supérieure des beaux-arts from circa 1858 to 1861.

Richard Pischel was an Indologist and linguist who earned his doctorate and habilitation at the University of Breslau, studying under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler and Albrecht Weber. He held professorships at Kiel (1875), Halle-Wittenberg (1885–1902), and Berlin (1902–1908).

Richard Polenberg was a historian of America who studied at Brooklyn College (BA) and Columbia University (PhD). He served as Professor of American History at Cornell University from 1966 to 2011 and as a Fulbright Visiting Professor at Hebrew University.

Richard S. Cohen specializes in Buddhist and religious studies, having studied under Luis Oscar Gómez and Walter M. Spink. He is an Associate Professor of South Asian Religious Literatures at the University of California, San Diego.
Richard Schechner studied at Cornell University, the University of Iowa, and Tulane University. Around 1967, he became a University Professor at the Tisch School of the Arts at New York University.

Richard Schmidt was an Indologist who completed his doctorate and habilitation at Halle-Wittenberg under Richard Pischel and Karl Friedrich Geldner. He served as Privatdozent at Halle-Wittenberg, librarian for the Deutsche Morgenländische Gesellschaft, and ordinary professor at Münster (1910).
Richard Shilleto was a scholar and linguist who studied at Repton School, Shrewsbury School (circa 1823–1828), and Trinity College, Cambridge (circa 1828–1832).

Richard Sorabji is a philosopher and Indologist who studied at Pembroke College, Oxford. He held academic posts at Cornell University (circa 1962–1970), King's College London (circa 1970–2000), and Gresham College (circa 2000–2006).

Richard Sproat is a computational linguist who studied at the University of California, San Diego and MIT. He held posts at UIUC (2003–2009), Oregon Health and Science University (2009–2012), and Google (2012).

Richard Sylvan was a philosopher who studied at Victoria University of Wellington and Princeton University. He held positions at the University of Sydney (circa 1963–1964) and the Australian National University (from 1971).

Richard Taupier works in history, archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies. He earned a doctorate and MS at UMass Amherst, where he became Associate Director of Research Development, and was a visiting lecturer at Smith College.

Richard W. Lariviere is an Indologist who studied under Ludo Rocher at the University of Pennsylvania (PhD). He served as dean at UT Austin, provost at Kansas, president of the University of Oregon, and president of the Field Museum.

Richard Wilhelm was a Sinologist who studied at the University of Tübingen. He served as a guest professor at Peking University (1923) and held the chair for Sinology at Goethe University Frankfurt from 1924, which he founded in 1925.

Richard von Garbe was an Indologist who earned his PhD at Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth and habilitation at Königsberg. He was a professor at Königsberg and held the chair of Indology at Tübingen from 1895 to 1927.

Richard von Glahn is a scholar of Sinology, history, and archaeology. He became a professor at the University of California, Los Angeles circa 1987 and was a visiting fellow at the University of Tokyo from 1988 to 1989.
Rigdzin Shikpo was a Buddhist and religious studies figure who studied under teachers Chögyam Trungpa and Khenpo Tsultrim Gyamtso Rinpoche.
Rigzin Lhundup was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who served as a professor at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara (attested in 1959 and 1987).
